name: Hatter
timbre: quick, bright, slightly nasal and reedy man's voice with a needling edge; goes thin and quavering under fear
pitch: high baritone to tenor, jumpy and sing-song, sudden spikes on a scored point
accent: London tradesman's English, light Cockney vowels straining upward toward genteel speech
reference_style: King of the stopped afternoon: rapid personal remarks, riddles without answers, triumphant word-play; always a beat quicker than the March Hare. In the witness box the same voice collapses into a trembling, whining tradesman ('I'm a poor man, your Majesty').
